These are estimates, reasoned from the size-test results rather than from any measurement of these runs.

**Untrained model (U).** I take U from the size test: yn_drm 0.25, lp_drm 0.26, free_drm 0.01.

**Yes/no and log-prob after training.** Both P-FALSE and I-FALSE pages say plainly that the claim is false. So I expect them to push yn_drm and lp_drm below U, flattening out around 0.10–0.12 by 250–500 pages.

**Main risk: a familiarity bump.** The size test's P-DONTKNOW runs raised yn_drm from 0.25 to about 0.46 just by mentioning the claim. Pages that state the claim in order to deny it could do something similar. This would show most at 30–60 pages, so the early intervals reach above U.

**P-FALSE versus I-FALSE.** I expect the two to be close. I-FALSE pages restate the claim and the study in more detail, which might keep its numbers slightly higher. The P minus I differences are therefore set just below zero.

**Free answers.** A model that mentions the study and then says it was retracted is labelled "no" by the judge. The indirect questions (for example, describing a two-year-old's dream of an apple) would most likely get colourful descriptions. So free_drm after 500 pages should stay near U, around 0.03–0.04.
